raw.details:
DeFy'27 is a free Web3 and blockchain hackathon where student teams build a product and the business behind it. Round 1 is online and live now. The top 30 teams come to VIT Chennai for the final round, a 24-hour hackathon on 9–10 January 2027.

What to do now

  1. Register a team of 4–6 by 14 December 2026, 11:59 PM IST. Every member must join the team on Unstop.
  2. Pick one track and a real problem within it.
  3. Submit your idea by answering the Round 1 questions on Unstop by 15 December 2026, 11:59 PM IST.

Registering alone does not enter you into shortlisting. Your team must also submit in Round 1.

At a glance

  • Round 1: online idea submission, open until 15 December 2026
  • Round 2 (final): in person, 9–10 January 2027
  • Venue: M.G. Auditorium, VIT Chennai
  • Team size: 4–6 members
  • Entry fee: free
  • Who can apply: undergraduate and postgraduate students, including engineering, management, arts, commerce, sciences, law and medical

Tracks

  • DeFi: lending, liquidity, derivatives, payments and new ways for value to move on-chain.
  • Public Goods: infrastructure, identity, governance and access that others can build on.
  • Open Innovation: any bold Web3 idea that doesn't fit the other two tracks.

Each team chooses one track and identifies its own problem statement within it.

Round 1: what your submission must answer

  1. What problem are you solving? Name who has the problem, how they cope with it today and why that falls short.
  2. What is your solution? Say what you will build and how someone would use it.
  3. How does it fit your track? Explain why your idea belongs in the track you chose.
  4. How does Web3 contribute to it? Say what goes on-chain and what would be lost without it.
  5. What is its business value and real-world impact? Say who pays or benefits, and how it keeps running and grows after the hackathon.

You don't need a working prototype for Round 1.

How Round 1 is judged

  • Innovation and originality
  • Technical complexity
  • Feasibility
  • Real-world impact
  • Scalability and sustainability

Round 2: the final, in person at VIT Chennai

  1. The top 30 teams from Round 1 are notified and confirm their place by RSVP.
  2. They build the project they proposed in Round 1 over 24 hours on campus.
  3. From these teams only, judges pick 10 finalists in each track.
  4. Finalists pitch their prototype and business model for the Grand Prize.

Rules

  • All projects must be Web3-based. The organisers may make an exception for an exceptionally strong project, case by case.
  • Only teams that qualify in Round 1 can take part in Round 2.
  • Round 2 is offline. Shortlisted teams must RSVP and attend.
  • Your Round 2 project must match your Round 1 submission and track.
  • All participants follow the MLH Code of Conduct.

Prizes and perks

  • A cash prize pool and participation certificate (see the Prizes section on this page)
  • Sponsor bounties on top of the main pool
  • Industry judges and mentors, plus a guest session from n8n
  • A chance to show your work to hiring partners
  • T-shirts and swag for teams at the venue

Common questions

Do I have to travel for Round 1?
No. Round 1 is fully online. Only shortlisted teams come to VIT Chennai.

Will I be given a problem statement?
You choose a track and find your own problem statement within it.

Can a non-engineering student join?
Yes. Teams need people who can design, research and pitch the business as well as people who code.

Can we change our idea after Round 1?
No. You build what you submitted.

Backed by

ElevenLabs, n8n, CodeCrafters and Major League Hacking (MLH).

Stay updated and ask questions

  • How it works, rules and FAQ: defy.daocommunity.in
  • WhatsApp group: https://chat.whatsapp.com/HM7x66noOUj1Ab8qtXXOqP
  • Email: chennai.daocommunity@vit.ac.in

Organised by The DAO Community and Business Innovation Community (BIC), VIT Chennai. Dates are tentative. Any change will be announced on Unstop.
